weaknesses.label: Banishing for Summons
weaknesses.why: Gullveig must banish cards from the hand or field to Special Summon from the Deck, and Alviss only works when banished by a Nordic Link Monster, so stopping banishes turns off those Summons.

weaknesses.label: Face-up monster effects
weaknesses.why: Gullveig's Link Summon effect, Vanadis's Level change and Gullinbursti's Summon effect are all activated monster effects on the field, so negating one stops the Synchro line.

weaknesses.label: Summons five or more
weaknesses.why: Gullveig can Summon up to three Nordic monsters from the Deck before the Synchro Summons, so the deck often reaches five Summons and loses its board to Nibiru.

weaknesses.label: Protected Aesir end board
weaknesses.why: Gullveig prevents targeting of the Aesir it points to and Svalinn negates the effects of all face-up cards you control, so non-targeting board breakers are needed going second.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Gullveig, Hlidskjalf or Tanngnjostr Special Summoning from the Deck, or Ivaldi's search.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every add from the Deck after the first, starving the deck of tuners and Nordic Relics.

answers.name: Artifact Lancea
answers.why: Neither player can banish cards, so Gullveig cannot pay its banishing effect and Alviss cannot trigger.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Gullveig's Link Summon effect or another face-up Nordic monster's effect before the Synchro Summon.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first key face-up monster effect, usually Gullveig or a tuner that sets up the Synchro Summon.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributes the Nordic board after Gullveig and the Synchro Summons have put five or more monsters on the field.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the protected Aesir board face-down without targeting, getting around Gullveig and Svalinn.

answers.name: Lightning Storm
answers.why: Destroys the Attack Position Aesir monsters, or destroys Svalinn and The Nordic Lights if the backrow is the problem.

profile.plan: Synchro climbs with little T.G. Tuners and Synchro Tuners, using Trident Launcher, Rocket Salamander and Hyper Librarian to keep the engine going, then Quick Synchro Summons on the opponent's turn into Shooting Star Dragon T.G. EX, Glaive Blaster and Halberd Cannon, backed by T.G. Close.

weaknesses.label: Searches and Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: T.G. Limiter Removal adds two T.G. monsters from the Deck, T.G. All Clear and T.G. Mighty Striker search, and T.G. Rocket Salamander and T.G. Trident Launcher Special Summon from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates those effects cuts the combo's fuel before it starts.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: T.G. Rocket Salamander's Tribute-to-Summon, T.G. Screw Serpent's revival and the Synchro Tuners' Quick Effects all activate on the field, so negating a face-up monster's effect strands the deck without materials.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons five or more times
weaknesses.why: A full climb from Trident Launcher and Over Dragonar Special Summons five or more monsters in one turn, so cards that punish that many Summons wipe the board mid-combo and leave nothing to Synchro with.

weaknesses.label: Everything it ends on is a Synchro
weaknesses.why: T.G. Halberd Cannon, T.G. Glaive Blaster and Shooting Star Dragon T.G. EX are all Synchro Monsters, so a card that forbids Synchro Summoning or negates their effects turns off the whole end board.

weaknesses.label: Recurs bodies from the Graveyard
weaknesses.why: T.G. Rocket Salamander, T.G. Over Dragonar and T.G. Trident Launcher Special Summon T.G. monsters from the GY and T.G. Star Guardian adds from it, so a floodgate that shuts off the GY stops the bodies coming back.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a negating Synchro board
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Halberd Cannon's Summon negation, Shooting Star Dragon T.G. EX, T.G. Glaive Blaster and the T.G. Close Counter Trap, so board breakers that cannot be responded to are needed to clear it.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates the add from T.G. Limiter Removal or T.G. All Clear and the Special Summon from the Deck of Rocket Salamander or Trident Launcher.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: After the first search it stops every further add and every Hyper Librarian draw, starving the climb.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Rocket Salamander or Screw Serpent, or a Synchro Tuner's Quick Effect Synchro Summon on your turn.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributes the whole board once the combo has Summoned five monsters, leaving no Synchro Material.

answers.name: Dimensional Barrier
answers.why: Calling Synchro stops every Synchro Summon and negates the effects of the face-up Synchro Monsters.

answers.name: Necrovalley
answers.why: Cards in the GY cannot be banished or moved, so Rocket Salamander, Over Dragonar, Trident Launcher and Star Guardian lose their GY plays.

answers.name: Forbidden Droplet
answers.why: Sends cards to the GY to negate Halberd Cannon and the other Synchro Monsters without giving them a chance to respond.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Synchro board and the set T.G. Close face-down at the end of the Battle Phase.

profile.plan: Synchro Climbs to a Level 10 Aesir boss by pairing a Nordic Tuner with two or more non-Tuners, ending on a 4000 ATK Odin that can make itself immune to Spells/Traps plus Thor negating all of the opponent's face-up monster effects, with the bosses reviving themselves from the GY in the End Phase and Fenrir/Jormungardr dumped on the opponent's field to burn them.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Thor's mass monster-effect negation, Odin's Spell/Trap immunity and draw, and Loki's Spell/Trap negation are all monster effects on the field, so negating a face-up monster's effects strips the boss the deck spent three monsters on.

weaknesses.label: End Phase revival from the GY
weaknesses.why: Odin, Thor and Loki only come back by banishing a Nordic Tuner from the GY in the End Phase, so banishing that Tuner or the Synchro itself in the GY removes the recursion the deck counts on.

weaknesses.label: Three monsters per Synchro
weaknesses.why: Odin, Thor and Loki each need a Nordic Tuner plus 2+ non-Tuners, so the deck Special Summons several times before its Level 10 lands and loses the field to Nibiru once it has Summoned five or more.

weaknesses.label: Spell/Trap-immune boss
weaknesses.why: Odin makes itself unaffected by Spell/Trap effects, so destruction and targeting Spells/Traps fail going second and the boss has to be Tributed away instead.

weaknesses.label: Ends on one big Synchro
weaknesses.why: The combo ends on a single Level 10 Aesir with a wall of ATK, so a board breaker such as Evenly Matched that banishes it face-down clears it without ever sending it to the GY to revive.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the Nordic Tuner's effect before the Synchro lands, or Thor's monster-effect negation once it is on the field.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates the first Aesir monster's effect on the field, which is where all of Odin, Thor and Loki's power sits.

answers.name: Dark Ruler No More
answers.why: Turns off every face-up Aesir's effects, including Odin's Spell/Trap immunity, so your Spells and Traps get through the boss.

answers.name: Skill Drain
answers.why: All of the deck's power is on-field monster effects, so paying 1000 LP leaves Odin, Thor and Loki as vanillas.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: A Tuner plus 2+ non-Tuners means five or more Summons, so Nibiru Tributes the whole field before the Level 10 Synchro lands.

answers.name: Called by the Grave
answers.why: Banishes the Nordic Tuner in the GY so the End Phase revival has nothing to banish to bring Odin, Thor or Loki back.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Aesir board face-down, which also stops it from being sent to the GY and reviving in the End Phase.

answers.name: Gameciel, the Sea Turtle Kaiju
answers.why: Tributing Odin ignores its Spell/Trap immunity and removes the 4000 ATK boss before it can protect itself.

profile.plan: Stalls with indestructible Timelords that cannot be destroyed by battle or card effects, using end-of-Battle Phase effects to burn, shuffle or bounce the opponent's cards, and protects them with Continuous Traps like Infinite Light.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Every Timelord's destruction protection and end-of-Battle Phase burn or shuffle are monster effects, so negating them (Infinite Impermanence, Dark Ruler No More, Skill Drain) leaves them as 0 ATK monsters with no protection.

weaknesses.label: Indestructible but not immune to Tribute or banish
weaknesses.why: All Timelords such as Michion and Sandaion cannot be destroyed by battle or card effects, so cards that Tribute them (Lava Golem) or banish them face-down (Evenly Matched) remove them without destroying.

weaknesses.label: Searches and Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Time Maiden adds a Timelord from the Deck and Infinite Light Special Summons from the Deck, so Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring stops both.

weaknesses.label: Relies on the Graveyard
weaknesses.why: Time Maiden banishes itself from the GY to Special Summon a Timelord, and Infinite Light Special Summons from the GY, so Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion negates those activations.

weaknesses.label: Relies on Continuous Traps
weaknesses.why: Infinite Light protects Timelords from targeting and Special Summons them, while Empty Machine and Infinite Machine recur them, so banishing or negating those Continuous Traps (Cosmic Cyclone, Royal Decree) strips the deck of its protection.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the entire Timelord board face-down at the end of the Battle Phase, bypassing their destruction protection and Infinite Light's targeting protection.

answers.name: Lava Golem
answers.why: Tribues two Timelords to Special Summon itself, removing indestructible monsters without destroying them.

answers.name: Dark Ruler No More
answers.why: Negates the effects of all face-up Timelords for the turn, turning off their destruction protection and end-of-Battle Phase burn.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates a Timelord's effects, stopping its destruction protection and its end-of-Battle Phase trigger.

answers.name: Skill Drain
answers.why: Negates all face-up monster effects, shutting off every Timelord's protection and burn effect.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Time Maiden's search from the Deck and Infinite Light's Special Summon from the Deck.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates Time Maiden's GY effect that Special Summons from the Deck and Infinite Light's Special Summon from the GY.

answers.name: Dimensional Barrier
answers.why: Declares Fairy, negating all Timelord effects and preventing any Fairy Special Summons for the turn.

profile.plan: Chips away while Symph Amplifire gathers Symphonic Counters, using Guitaar's discard, DJJ and Guitariss to Special Summon Symphonic Warriors from the Deck and hand, then tunes them into the Synchro Pendulum Rockks and recycles Pendulum Monsters from the Extra Deck.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Guitaar's Pendulum effect and DJJ's Summon effect both Special Summon a Symphonic Warrior from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates that Summon leaves the deck without a body to Synchro with.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Guitaar's revive, DJJ's Summon effect, Synthess's name copy and Rockks's destroy are all face-up monster effects, so negating one of them ends the Synchro play early.

weaknesses.label: Symph Amplifire in the Field Zone
weaknesses.why: Rockks can only destroy a card, Guitariss can only Special Summon herself and DJJ can only Summon face-up while Symph Amplifire is in the Field Zone, so removing the Field Spell cuts every payoff.

weaknesses.label: Every monster is WIND Machine
weaknesses.why: Guitaar, DJJ, Guitariss, Rockks, Piaano, Basses, Drumss and Synthess all share one Type and Attribute, so a floodgate limiting one Type or Attribute leaves the deck with a single monster on the field.

weaknesses.label: The whole deck is Machine
weaknesses.why: Guitaar, DJJ, Rockks, Piaano, Basses, Drumss and Synthess are all Machine, so System Down banishes the entire field and Graveyard at once.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a Rockks board
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Rockks plus the Pendulum Monsters it keeps adding back, so a board breaker that clears the whole field gets through its destruction effect.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Guitaar's Pendulum effect or DJJ's Summon effect before a Symphonic Warrior hits the field.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Guitaar's revive, DJJ's Special Summon or Synthess's name copy on the field.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first Symphonic Warrior monster effect, stopping the Synchro Summon.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Symph Amplifire, turning off Rockks's destroy, Guitariss's free Special Summon and DJJ's face-up Summon.

answers.name: Gozen Match
answers.why: Every Symphonic Warrior is WIND, so the deck can only control one monster at a time.

answers.name: Rivalry of Warlords
answers.why: Every Symphonic Warrior is Machine, so the deck can only control one monster at a time.

answers.name: System Down
answers.why: Banishes every Machine monster the deck controls and has in the Graveyard, including Rockks and its Tuners.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Rockks board face-down without targeting, getting past its destruction effect.

profile.plan: Searches Change Quick-Play Spells and Masked HERO pieces with Furnace, Dusk Crow and Miracle Ejector, then Mask Changes into Dark Law and Atomic, ending on Dark Law's GY banish/hand rip plus Atomic's revival and a set Change Spell.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Furnace adds a Change Spell or Polymerization from the Deck, Dusk Crow adds a Masked HERO from the Deck, and Miracle Ejector adds a Spell/Trap from the Deck, so Ash Blossom or Droll stops the engine before the Fusions.

weaknesses.label: Quick-Play Mask Change
weaknesses.why: Dark Law and Atomic are made with Change Quick-Play Spells, so Anti-Spell Fragrance forbids activating them and leaves the deck unable to Mask Change.
phrases: Quick-Play Spell Cards cannot be activated

weaknesses.label: Fusion Summons from Extra Deck
weaknesses.why: Dark Law and Atomic are only Fusion Summoned by Mask Change or Polymerization, so Dimensional Barrier declaring Fusion stops those Summons and negates the Fusion monsters.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Dark Law's hand rip and Atomic's revival are face-up monster effects, so Infinite Impermanence or Dark Ruler No More negates them.

weaknesses.label: Graveyard recursion
weaknesses.why: Furnace Special Summons itself from the GY and Dusk Crow needs a HERO in the GY to banish, so D.D. Crow removing those GY cards cuts the recursion.

weaknesses.label: Ends on Dark Law board
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Dark Law plus Atomic and a set Change Spell, so Evenly Matched banishes the field without sending cards to the GY and gets around Dark Law.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Furnace, Dusk Crow or Miracle Ejector adding cards from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every search after the first, including Furnace, Dusk Crow, Miracle Ejector and Legacy's draw.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Dark Law's hand rip or Atomic's revival on the field.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes Furnace from the GY before it can Special Summon itself, or removes the HERO Dusk Crow wants to banish.

answers.name: Anti-Spell Fragrance
answers.why: Stops Mask Change being activated as a Quick-Play Spell, cutting off Dark Law and Atomic.

answers.name: Dimensional Barrier
answers.why: Declaring Fusion prevents the Mask Change and Polymerization Fusion Summons and negates Dark Law and Atomic.

answers.name: Dark Ruler No More
answers.why: Negates all face-up monster effects, turning off Dark Law's banish/hand rip and Atomic's protection.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Dark Law/Atomic board face-down without sending the cards to the GY.

profile.plan: Gusto wins by using its monsters' effects when they are sent to the GY to Special Summon more Gusto monsters from the Deck, then Synchro Summoning into Daigusto Sphreez and Daigusto Laplampilica to control the board with battle damage redirection and targeting protection.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Gulldo, Griffin, Egul, Winda, Kamui, Falco, Squirro, Tailwind and Laplampilica all Special Summon monsters from the Deck, so Ash Blossom negates the first one and ends the turn.

weaknesses.label: Triggers when sent to the GY
weaknesses.why: Gulldo, Egul, Winda, Falco and Squirro only recruit from the Deck when they are sent to the GY, so Dimension Shifter banishes them instead and the effects never trigger.

weaknesses.label: Uses the GY as a resource
weaknesses.why: Daigusto Gulldos, Caam, Contact with Gusto and Blessings for Gusto shuffle Gusto monsters from the GY into the Deck, so banishing those monsters or negating GY effects stops the recursion.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Gusto Vedir, Caam, Musto, Pilica and Reeze all use ignition effects on the field, so Infinite Impermanence or Effect Veiler negates the first one and stops the combo.

weaknesses.label: Summons many monsters
weaknesses.why: A full Gusto combo Special Summons five or more monsters through Laplampilica and the recruit effects, so Nibiru, the Primal Being can Tribute the whole board.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a Synchro board
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Daigusto Sphreez, which redirects battle damage and cannot be destroyed by battle, and Laplampilica protecting other Synchros, so non-targeting board breakers like Evenly Matched are needed.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates the Deck Special Summons from Gulldo, Griffin, Egul and other Gusto recruiters.

answers.name: Dimension Shifter
answers.why: Banishes monsters sent to the GY instead, so Gulldo, Egul and the other GY triggers never happen.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Gusto Vedir's send from Deck to GY or Caam's draw, ending the turn early.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributues the entire board after the combo has Summoned five monsters.

answers.name: Necrovalley
answers.why: Stops effects that would move cards from the GY, shutting off the shuffling from Gulldos, Caam and Contact with Gusto.

answers.name: Abyss Dweller
answers.why: Prevents any GY effects, so Gulldo, Egul and the shuffling effects cannot activate.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Synchro board face-down, bypassing Sphreez's battle protection and Laplampilica's targeting protection.

answers.name: Gameciel, the Sea Turtle Kaiju
answers.why: Tributues Daigusto Sphreez, which cannot be destroyed by battle and redirects damage.

profile.plan: Uses Isolde and the Noble Knight/Infernoble Knight engine to equip Warrior monsters with Noble Arms, Synchro or Link Summon, and ends on Infernoble Knight Emperor Charles and Emperor Charles the Great with Equip Spell-backed negation.

weaknesses.label: Deck-to-hand searches
weaknesses.why: Isolde adds a Warrior, Heritage of the Chalice and Borz add Noble Arms, and Roland and Durendal add cards from the Deck, so Ash Blossom or Droll stops the first search.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons from Deck
weaknesses.why: Isolde, Medraut and Merlin Special Summon a Warrior or Noble Knight from the Deck, so Ash Blossom on that Summon leaves the board empty.

weaknesses.label: Relies on the GY
weaknesses.why: Oliver, Ogier and Maugis equip themselves from the GY while Roland, Durendal and Excaliburn use it, so Called by the Grave or Dimension Shifter cuts the recursion.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on field
weaknesses.why: Medraut, Borz, Drystan and Emperor Charles all need their face-up monster effects to resolve, so Infinite Impermanence or Effect Veiler on the first one ends the turn.

weaknesses.label: Equip Spell end board
weaknesses.why: Emperor Charles the Great negates by sending an Equip Spell and the Noble Arms protect the Warriors, so Harpie's Feather Duster destroys the Equip Spells and turns off that protection and negation.

weaknesses.label: Long Special Summon chains
weaknesses.why: The Isolde into Medraut into Infernoble Synchro line Special Summons five or more monsters, so Nibiru can Tribute the board before the Equip Spells are set up.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Isolde's search or Special Summon from the Deck, Heritage of the Chalice, Borz and Roland's Deck adds, and Medraut or Merlin's Deck Summons.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: After the first search, it stops every further add from the Deck, cutting off Isolde, Heritage, Borz and Roland.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Isolde, Medraut or Borz on the field, stopping the search or Equip Spell setup.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first Noble Knight or Infernoble Knight monster effect on the field, such as Medraut or Borz.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tribues the whole board once the Isolde into Medraut into Synchro line has Summoned five or more monsters.

answers.name: Dimension Shifter
answers.why: Makes every card sent to the GY banished instead, so the Infernoble Knights cannot equip themselves from the GY and Isolde's Equip Spells never stay there.

answers.name: Called by the Grave
answers.why: Banishes a key Infernoble Knight or Equip Spell from the GY and negates its effect, stopping the equip recursion.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys the Noble Arms and Infernoble Arms Equip Spells, stripping Emperor Charles the Great of its negation cost and the Warriors of their protection.

profile.plan: Meklord wins by destroying its own monsters with card effects to Special Summon Meklord Emperors from the hand or Deck, then equipping the opponent's Synchro Monsters to grow their ATK and ending on Emperor Wisel negating Spells with Synchro Absorption protecting from destruction.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Nucleus Infinity Core adds a Meklord Spell/Trap and Assembly adds a Meklord monster from the Deck, so Ash Blossom or Droll & Lock Bird stops the engine's first search.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on field
weaknesses.why: Nucleus Infinity Core, Deployer Obbligato and Emperor Wisel all use face-up monster effects, so Infinite Impermanence negates the first one and ends the turn.

weaknesses.label: Needs the Graveyard
weaknesses.why: Emperor Wisel, Granel and Skiel only Special Summon themselves when a monster is destroyed by card effect and sent to the GY, and Triskelion and Eradicator need Meklords in the GY, so Dimension Shifter's banished instead cuts both off.

weaknesses.label: All monsters are Machine
weaknesses.why: Every Meklord monster is Machine, so System Down banishes the whole field and GY.

weaknesses.label: Relies on Field Spells
weaknesses.why: Assembly searches and destroys, Fortissimo Special Summons Army monsters and Fortress protects the Emperors, so Harpie's Feather Duster clears the support the deck sits on.

weaknesses.label: Protected Emperor bosses
weaknesses.why: Emperor Wisel negates Spell activations and Synchro Absorption negates destruction, so a Kaiju Tribute or Evenly Matched's banish gets rid of them without triggering those protections.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Nucleus Infinity Core's or Assembly's add from the Deck, and Deployer Obbligato's Special Summon from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every search after the first, so Nucleus and Assembly cannot keep adding Meklord cards.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Nucleus Infinity Core, Deployer Obbligato or Emperor Wisel on the field before their effects resolve.

answers.name: Dimension Shifter
answers.why: Makes every card sent to the GY banished instead, so the Emperors cannot be Summoned by their own effects and Triskelion and Eradicator lose their GY fuel.

answers.name: System Down
answers.why: Banishes every Machine monster the deck controls and all Meklords in its GY.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Clears Assembly, Fortissimo and Fortress, cutting off searches, free Summons and Emperor protection.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Emperor board face-down without destroying it, so Emperor Wisel and Synchro Absorption cannot negate it.

answers.name: Gameciel, the Sea Turtle Kaiju
answers.why: Tributing Emperor Wisel with a Kaiju removes it without activating a Spell or destroying it.

profile.plan: Tribute Summons Steelswarm bosses and grinds with a wall of Trap Cards — Infection searching every turn, Wave and Terminus trading its own monster for the opponent's cards — while Pandemic shields the face-up lswarm monsters from Spells and Traps.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Infestation Infection adds a monster from the Deck to the hand and Infestation Tool sends one from the Deck to the GY, so a hand trap that negates Deck effects cuts the engine's fuel and its GY setup at once.

weaknesses.label: Everything needs a Tribute Summon
weaknesses.why: First Step Towards Infestation and Infestation Wave only work with a face-up Tribute Summoned Steelswarm, so a floodgate that forbids Tributing stops the Summon and leaves both cards with no legal cost.

weaknesses.label: The engine is all Trap Cards
weaknesses.why: Infestation Infection, Terminus, Ripples, Tool and Wave are all Traps that must stay on the field to resolve, so backrow removal or Trap-effect negation takes out the whole grind game.

weaknesses.label: Revives from the Graveyard
weaknesses.why: Infestation Ripples Special Summons a Steelswarm from the GY after Infestation Tool puts it there, so banishing that monster from the GY leaves Ripples with no target.

weaknesses.label: Protection only against Spells and Traps
weaknesses.why: Infestation Pandemic makes face-up lswarm monsters unaffected by Spell/Trap effects only, so a monster effect that Tributes or otherwise removes the Steelswarm still takes away the body that Wave, Terminus and First Step need as their cost.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Infestation Infection's add from the Deck or Infestation Tool's send from the Deck, ending the search loop and the GY setup.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every add and draw after the first, shutting off Infection, Tool and the draw of First Step Towards Infestation.

answers.name: Mask of Restrict
answers.why: Neither player can Tribute, so no Steelswarm is ever Tribute Summoned and First Step and Infestation Wave lose their cost.

answers.name: Royal Decree
answers.why: Negates every Trap effect on the field, which is the deck's entire engine — Infection, Terminus, Ripples, Tool and Wave.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys the Continuous Trap engine and the whole set backrow in one card going second.

answers.name: Twin Twisters
answers.why: Destroys Infestation Infection before it can shuffle and search, and clears a second set Trap.

answers.name: Skill Drain

answers.name: Mask of Restrict

answers.name: Summon Limit

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster

answers.name: Lightning Storm

answers.name: Called by the Grave
answers.why: Banishes Legion the Fiend Jester from the GY and negates its search effect.

profile.plan: Dragon Ravine and Romulus set up equipping Dragon Tuners from the Deck and GY to Winged Beast starters, then Synchro Summon Level 6-10 Dragon monsters like Areadbhair and Ascalon, ending on negations and banishing removal.

weaknesses.label: Deck searches and summons
weaknesses.why: Dragon Ravine, Romulus, Gae Dearg, Glow and Whirlwind all add or Special Summon from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates those effects stops the setup before the equips happen.

weaknesses.label: Normal Summon starters
weaknesses.why: Dux, Senatus and Legionnaire need their Normal Summon effects to equip Tuners from the GY or Deck, so negating a face-up monster's effect ends the first play.

weaknesses.label: Field Spell Dragon Ravine
weaknesses.why: Dragon Ravine is the main search and send engine and Romulus adds it, so destroying or banishing the Field Spell cuts the deck's first setup.

weaknesses.label: GY setup cut off
weaknesses.why: Dux, Legionnaire, Vajrayana and Barcha equip Tuners from the GY while Remus and Glow need the GY, so cards that banish everything sent there leave no targets for those plays.

weaknesses.label: Mixed Types for Synchro
weaknesses.why: Dux and Senatus are Winged Beast non-Tuners while the Tuners are Dragon, so forcing one Type stops both from staying on the field together for a Synchro Summon.

weaknesses.label: Negating end board
weaknesses.why: Areadbhair and Georgius negate monster and Spell/Trap effects, so a board breaker that clears or silences the board is needed going second.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Dragon Ravine, Romulus, Gae Dearg, Glow or Whirlwind when they search or Summon from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every search after the first, cutting off the Ravine, Romulus and Gae Dearg chain.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Dux, Senatus or Romulus on the field before they equip or search.

answers.name: Dimension Shifter
answers.why: Cards sent to the GY are banished instead, so Dux, Remus and the equip-from-GY plays have no targets.

answers.name: Macro Cosmos
answers.why: Banishes every card sent to the GY, shutting off the deck's GY equips and recursion while it stays on the field.

answers.name: Rivalry of Warlords
answers.why: Forces each player to one Type, so a Dragon Tuner and a Winged Beast non-Tuner cannot stay on the field together.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Dragon Ravine and the equipped Tuners in the Spell & Trap Zone, cutting the search and Synchro setup.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Areadbhair/Georgius board and the backrow after the Battle Phase, bypassing their negations.

profile.plan: A slow Spellcaster Synchro deck that searches and Special Summons Fortune Lady monsters from the Deck, uses their Level-gaining and banishing effects to Synchro Summon Fortune Lady Every, and grinds with Every's Standby banish and End Phase revival plus Fortune Vision's protection.

weaknesses.label: Searches and summons from Deck
weaknesses.why: Fortune Vision adds a Fortune Lady card and Fortune Lady Calling Special Summons one from the Deck, while Fortune Lady Light Special Summons one when it leaves the field by card effect; Ash Blossom negates any of those.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Fortune Lady Water's draw, Fortune Lady Past's Level change, Solitaire Magician's destruction and Fortune Lady Every's banish all activate on the field, so a hand trap that negates a face-up monster stops the key play.

weaknesses.label: All monsters are Spellcasters
weaknesses.why: Every Fortune Lady and Solitaire Magician is a Spellcaster, so There Can Be Only One reduces the deck to a single monster and blocks its Synchro climbs.

weaknesses.label: Mixed Attributes
weaknesses.why: Fortune Lady monsters are LIGHT, DARK, WATER, FIRE, EARTH and WIND, so Gozen Match forces the deck to one Attribute and stops it assembling the different monsters it needs.

weaknesses.label: Banishes its own Spellcasters
weaknesses.why: Fortune Lady Past banishes Spellcasters from the hand, field and GY to change Levels and Fortune Lady Every banishes a Spellcaster from the GY to revive, so Artifact Lancea stops both by forbidding banishes.

weaknesses.label: Relies on Continuous Spell and Counter Trap
weaknesses.why: Fortune Vision searches and grants destruction protection while Bending Destiny negates Spells/Traps or Normal Summons, so backrow removal like Harpie's Feather Duster clears them before the board is protected.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Fortune Vision's search, Fortune Lady Calling's Special Summon from the Deck, or Fortune Lady Light's Deck Summon.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Fortune Lady Water's draw, Fortune Lady Past's Level change, or Fortune Lady Every's banish.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates Fortune Lady Water or Fortune Lady Past before it can set up the Synchro or draw.

answers.name: There Can Be Only One
answers.why: All the deck's monsters are Spellcasters, so it can only keep one on the field.

answers.name: Gozen Match
answers.why: The deck uses Fortune Ladies of many Attributes, so it is forced down to one Attribute.

answers.name: Artifact Lancea
answers.why: Stops Fortune Lady Past and Fortune Lady Every from banishing Spellcasters.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Fortune Vision and set Bending Destiny before they protect the board.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Fortune Lady Every board and backrow face-down, getting past its protection and revival.

profile.plan: Loops Tuners out of the Graveyard — Launcher, Blaster, Archer, Planter and Doctor all Special Summon themselves back — to climb into WATER Synchro Monsters such as with Harpooner as material, so the deck wins by repeatedly rebuilding a WATER Synchro board from the GY each turn.

weaknesses.label: Self-Summons from the Graveyard
weaknesses.why: Launcher, Blaster, Archer, Planter and Doctor all Special Summon themselves from the GY, so banishing one of them from the GY before its effect resolves leaves nothing to Summon.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects in the GY
weaknesses.why: Every play starts with a GY effect of Launcher, Blaster, Archer, Planter or Doctor, so negating the effects of monsters in the GY turns the whole engine off.

weaknesses.label: Needs WATER monsters in the GY
weaknesses.why: Launcher, Blaster, Archer, Planter and Doctor can only Summon themselves while WATER monsters are in the GY, so anything that banishes cards instead of sending them there leaves the GY empty and the deck with no plays.

weaknesses.label: Mills its own Deck
weaknesses.why: Planter's whole effect is sending the top card of the Deck to the GY and Special Summoning itself, so a hand trap that negates that send stops the engine's cheapest starter.

weaknesses.label: Loops many Special Summons
weaknesses.why: The deck revives Launcher, Blaster, Archer, Planter and Doctor over and over to climb Synchro Monsters, so it reaches five or more Summons in one turn and loses to cards that punish that.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a WATER Synchro board
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Synchro Monsters made with Harpooner and the revived Tuners, so a board breaker that clears the field gets through the negations Harpooner sets up.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Planter's send from the Deck to the GY, cutting off the cheapest way to get the engine going.

answers.name: Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion
answers.why: Negates the effect that Special Summons a Fishborg from the GY, stopping Launcher, Blaster, Archer, Planter or Doctor.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes a Fishborg from the GY in response to its own revival effect, so nothing comes back.

answers.name: Called by the Grave
answers.why: Banishes a Fishborg in the GY and negates its effects for the turn, ending the loop.

answers.name: Dimension Shifter
answers.why: Everything sent to the GY is banished instead, so the deck never has WATER monsters in the GY to revive.

answers.name: Macro Cosmos
answers.why: Banishes all cards instead of sending them to the GY, leaving the GY effects of every Fishborg with nothing to work with.

answers.name: Soul Drain
answers.why: Negates the effects of monsters in the GY, which is where Launcher, Blaster, Archer, Planter and Doctor all activate.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributes the field once the GY loop has Special Summoned five or more monsters for the Synchro climb.

profile.plan: Reacts to the opponent's Special Summons with 'C' hand traps: Maxx "C" draws, Retaliating "C" locks the GY, and Contact/Flying "C" Special Summon to the opponent's field to lock Extra Deck Summons, while Super Armored Robot Armed Black Iron "C" clears the board.

weaknesses.label: Relies on opponent Special Summons
weaknesses.why: Maxx "C", Contact "C", Flying "C", Sneaky "C" and Confronting "C" only trigger when the opponent Special Summons, so a floodgate that forbids Special Summoning leaves them dead in hand.

weaknesses.label: Maxx C's draw engine
weaknesses.why: Maxx "C" draws a card every time the opponent Special Summons, so a hand trap that negates the draw, like Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring, cuts off the deck's main resource.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects negatable by quick-plays
weaknesses.why: Maxx "C" and Shiny Black "C" are monster effects that can be negated by quick-play spells such as Called by the Grave and Crossout Designator before they resolve.

weaknesses.label: Cards sent to the GY
weaknesses.why: Maxx "C" sends itself to the GY as a cost and Shiny Black "C" needs the GY, so effects that banish cards instead of sending them there, like Dimension Shifter and Macro Cosmos, turn the deck off.

weaknesses.label: Contact and Flying C lock
weaknesses.why: Contact "C" and Flying "C" Special Summon themselves to your field and stop Fusion/Synchro/Xyz/Link or Xyz Summons while face-up, so flipping them face-down with Book of Moon removes the lock.

weaknesses.label: Sneaky C's End Phase wipe
weaknesses.why: Sneaky "C" flips face-up during the End Phase and destroys all Special Summoned monsters, so banishing it before then with Evenly Matched stops the wipe.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Maxx "C"'s draw effect when it resolves.

answers.name: Called by the Grave
answers.why: Banishes Maxx "C" from the GY and negates it, and can also negate Shiny Black "C" or Retaliating "C" in the GY.

answers.name: Crossout Designator
answers.why: Banishes a copy of Maxx "C" from your Deck to negate it.

answers.name: Dimension Shifter
answers.why: Cards sent to the GY are banished instead, so Maxx "C" cannot pay its cost and Shiny Black "C" never reaches the GY.

answers.name: Macro Cosmos
answers.why: Continuously banishes all cards sent to the GY, turning off Maxx "C" and Shiny Black "C".

answers.name: Vanity's Emptiness
answers.why: Neither player can Special Summon, so the "C" hand traps cannot Special Summon themselves and Maxx "C" never gets a draw.

answers.name: Book of Moon
answers.why: Flips Contact "C" or Flying "C" face-down, turning off their Extra Deck lock.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes Sneaky "C" and the rest of the opponent's board before the End Phase wipe.

profile.plan: Uses Infernity Sage, Beetle and Launcher to empty the hand and fill the GY, then revives Necromancer, Mirage or Launcher targets for Synchro Summons into Doom Archfiend or Doom Dragon while setting Infernity Barrier and Suppression.

weaknesses.label: Searches and Summons from Deck
weaknesses.why: Infernity Beetle Special Summons copies from the Deck, Paranoia Summons from the Deck, Sage sends from the Deck to the GY and Pawn places cards from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates Deck effects stops the setup.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Necromancer, Mirage, Beetle and Doom Archfiend all need their face-up monster effects to start or extend, so negating a monster's effect on the field ends the turn.

weaknesses.label: Summons many monsters
weaknesses.why: Launcher, Necromancer, Beetle and Mirage Special Summon repeatedly, so once the combo has Summoned five or more monsters Nibiru Tributes the board.

weaknesses.label: All monsters are DARK
weaknesses.why: Every Infernity monster is DARK, so a floodgate that negates DARK monster effects on the field and in the GY turns off Necromancer, Mirage and Doom Archfiend at once.

weaknesses.label: Graveyard recursion
weaknesses.why: Necromancer, Launcher, Mirage and General Special Summon from the GY, so a card that shuts off the GY or forbids moving cards out of it stops the combo.

weaknesses.label: Relies on Set Traps
weaknesses.why: Infernity Barrier and Suppression are Set Traps that negate your plays, so Spell/Trap removal clears them before you commit.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Beetle's Summon from the Deck, Paranoia's Summon from the Deck, or Sage sending from the Deck to the GY.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Necromancer, Beetle or Doom Archfiend on the field before the combo extends.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributes the board after Launcher, Necromancer and Beetle have Summoned five or more monsters.

answers.name: Shadow-Imprisoning Mirror
answers.why: Negates the DARK monster effects of Necromancer, Mirage, Doom Archfiend and the GY Infernity monsters.

answers.name: Skill Drain
answers.why: Negates the face-up field effects the deck uses to revive and extend.

answers.name: Soul Drain
answers.why: Negates the GY and banished monster effects it relies on, including Necromancer and General.

answers.name: Necrovalley
answers.why: Stops cards moving out of the GY and forbids banishing from it, cutting off Necromancer, Launcher and Mirage.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Synchro board and the Set Barrier and Suppression at the end of the Battle Phase.

profile.plan: It is not really a combo deck at all: the Forbidden cards are a toolkit of Quick-Play Spells held in hand that halve and negate the opponent's monster effects, protect your own monsters, or freeze a battle, used to blunt or break whatever board the opponent builds.

weaknesses.label: Spell Card activations
weaknesses.why: Forbidden Droplet, Chalice, Lance and Dress all resolve as Spell Cards, so a Counter Trap that negates a Spell's activation stops any of them before its negation or protection ever applies.

weaknesses.label: Quick-Play Spells from the hand
weaknesses.why: Forbidden Droplet, Chalice, Lance, Dress and Crown are Quick-Play Spells meant to be activated straight from the hand on either turn, so a floodgate that forces Spell Cards to be Set first turns the whole toolkit off.

weaknesses.label: Aims at one face-up monster
weaknesses.why: Forbidden Chalice, Lance, Dress and Crown all target a single face-up monster, so a monster that cannot be targeted or is unaffected by Spell effects ignores the negate-and-halve completely.

weaknesses.label: Has to sit in the hand
weaknesses.why: Every Forbidden card only works while it waits in the hand for the right moment (Droplet even needs other cards in hand to send), so hand disruption that reveals and discards Spells strips the deck of its entire toolkit.

answers.name: Anti-Spell Fragrance
answers.why: Forces Spell Cards to be Set before they can be activated, so no Forbidden Quick-Play can be used from the hand on the opponent's turn.

answers.name: Solemn Judgment
answers.why: Negates the activation of any Forbidden Spell and destroys it.

answers.name: Dark Bribe
answers.why: Negates the activation of the Forbidden Spell and destroys it, at the cost of one draw.

answers.name: Eradicator Epidemic Virus
answers.why: Declares Spell, discards every Spell in the opponent's hand and forbids Spell activation, emptying the Forbidden toolkit.

answers.name: Mind Crush
answers.why: Names a Forbidden card and makes the opponent discard every copy of it from the hand.

profile.plan: Searches Equip Spells with a Level 7 Synchro, climbs into bigger Synchro monsters and uses Equip Spells for negation and protection, ending on a Synchro board with Equip Spells and Extra Deck Special Summons.

weaknesses.label: Equip Spell search from Deck
weaknesses.why: The Level 7 Synchro reveals 3 Equip Spells from the Deck and adds 1 to the hand, so a hand trap that negates that add stops the deck from finding its Equip Spells.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: The Synchro monsters start or extend the combo with face-up monster effects, so negating one of those monsters ends the Synchro climb.

weaknesses.label: Extra Deck Synchro Summons
weaknesses.why: The board is built by Synchro Summoning and by Special Summoning Synchro monsters from the Extra Deck, so locking Extra Deck Summons stops it.

weaknesses.label: Relies on Equip Spells
weaknesses.why: The deck equips up to 3 Equip Spells and uses them to negate, banishes Equip Spells from the GY to survive, and an Equip Spell is its battle protection, so a floodgate that stops Spell Cards cuts its protection and interaction.

weaknesses.label: Equip Spells in the GY
weaknesses.why: The deck equips Equip Spells from the GY, banishes an Equip Spell from the GY instead of being destroyed and returns Equip Cards from the GY, so banishing those Equip Spells takes away its protection and recursion.

weaknesses.label: Equip Spells on the field
weaknesses.why: The negation costs an Equip Spell on the field, an Equip Spell keeps the equipped monster alive and the Synchro protection depends on another Synchro, so backrow removal strips the Equip Spells and opens the board.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates the Level 7 Synchro's Equip Spell add from the Deck, the deck's main search.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first Synchro monster's search or the bigger Synchro's equip-and-negate effect on the field.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates a face-up Synchro monster before it can search, equip Equip Spells or negate effects.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributes the board after the deck has Summoned five or more monsters during its Synchro climb.

answers.name: Dimensional Barrier
answers.why: Declares Synchro, preventing the deck's Synchro Summons and negating the effects of its Synchro monsters.

answers.name: Anti-Spell Fragrance
answers.why: Forces Equip Spells to be Set before activation, slowing the Equip Spell engine and its negation setup.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes an Equip Spell from the GY before it can be equipped from there or banished for destruction protection.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys the Equip Spells on the field, removing the negation cost and the equipped monster's protection.

profile.plan: A stun/beatdown deck: it searches Iron Core and Special Summons Level 4 Koa'ki Meiru monsters with Urnight and Supplier, keeping them alive through the End Phase by revealing or sending Iron Core, ending on 1900 ATK bodies with Quick Effect negates, Drago's LIGHT/DARK Special Summon lock and set Traps.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Diamond Core and Core Transport Unit add Iron Core, Supplier adds Iron Core or a card listing it, and Urnight Special Summons from the Deck; a hand trap that negates those Deck effects stops the first play.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Guardian, Overload, Wall and Sandman are face-up Quick Effects that Tribute themselves to negate, and Doom negates LIGHT/DARK Main Phase effects; negating those monsters leaves the board without interaction.

weaknesses.label: Iron Core must reach the GY
weaknesses.why: Urgent Synthesis returns Iron Core from the GY and many End Phase maintenance costs send it there, so effects that banish cards instead of sending them to the GY stop those costs and turn the monsters into End Phase self-destructions.

weaknesses.label: Ends on Quick Effect negates
weaknesses.why: Going second you face Guardian, Overload, Wall and Sandman plus Iron Core Luster, so board breakers that stop the opponent responding get through their negation.

weaknesses.label: Set Traps and Continuous Spells
weaknesses.why: Iron Core Luster and Automatic Laser are set Traps and Core Transport Unit, Core Overclock and Iron Core Specimen Lab are Continuous/Field Spells that fuel the deck; backrow removal strips them.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Diamond Core's search, Supplier's add and Urnight's Special Summon from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every add from the Deck after the first, cutting off Diamond Core, Supplier and Core Transport Unit searches.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Urnight, Supplier or one of the Quick Effect Koa'ki Meiru monsters before it can Tribute itself.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first face-up Koa'ki Meiru monster effect, such as Urnight's Special Summon or Guardian's negation.

answers.name: Dark Ruler No More
answers.why: Negates all face-up Koa'ki Meiru monster effects and cannot be responded to, so Guardian, Overload, Wall and Sandman cannot negate.

answers.name: Forbidden Droplet
answers.why: Sends cards to the GY to negate multiple Koa'ki Meiru monsters, and they cannot respond, breaking the Quick Effect negation board.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Iron Core Luster, Automatic Laser, Core Reinforcement and the deck's Continuous/Field Spells.

answers.name: Dimension Shifter
answers.why: Makes every card sent to the GY banished instead, so Iron Core can't be sent for maintenance or Urgent Synthesis and Supplier's Rock trigger never happens.

profile.plan: Sets Pendulum scales to Pendulum Summon several Spellcasters, accumulates Spell Counters on Magical Citadel of Endymion and its Pendulum monsters, and ends on Endymion, the Mighty Master of Magic with a Spell Counter to negate and protect, plus Selene to revive Spellcasters.

weaknesses.label: Spell Counter engine
weaknesses.why: Magical Citadel of Endymion, Servant of Endymion and Magister of Endymion only gain Spell Counters when Spell Cards are activated, so a floodgate that stops Spell Cards from being activated shuts off every counter and the Pendulum Summons that need them.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Spell Power Mastery, Endymion Empire, Regulus and Verre all add cards from the Deck to the hand, so a hand trap that negates the add strips the deck of its key pieces.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Selene, Magister and Genni use Quick Effects on the field to Special Summon, and Endymion, the Mighty Master of Magic negates with an on-field effect, so negating a face-up monster's effect stops the combo.

weaknesses.label: Pendulum Summons many monsters
weaknesses.why: The deck sets scales and Pendulum Summons several Spellcasters at once, so a card that punishes five or more Summons Tributes the whole board.

weaknesses.label: Field and Continuous Spells
weaknesses.why: Magical Citadel of Endymion stores and recycles Spell Counters while Endymion's Lab and Endymion Empire protect the board, so removing the backrow cuts the counter supply and the protection.

weaknesses.label: Protected negating boss
weaknesses.why: Endymion, the Mighty Master of Magic with a Spell Counter cannot be targeted or destroyed and negates Spell/Trap activations, so board breakers that don't target and negate monster effects are needed to clear it.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Spell Power Mastery, Endymion Empire or Regulus adding from the Deck, and the Deck Special Summons of Servant and Magister.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Selene, Magister or Genni's Quick Effect Special Summon, or Endymion, the Mighty Master of Magic before it gains a Spell Counter.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributues the whole Pendulum Summoned board once five monsters have been Summoned.

answers.name: Anti-Spell Fragrance
answers.why: Spell Cards must be Set first, so no Spell resolves to place Spell Counters and the Pendulum effects that need them stop.

answers.name: There Can Be Only One
answers.why: Every Endymion monster is a Spellcaster, so this locks them to a single monster on the field.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the board without targeting, getting past Mighty Master's protection.

answers.name: Dark Ruler No More
answers.why: Negates all of the opponent's monster effects without targeting, so Mighty Master cannot negate it or protect itself.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys Magical Citadel of Endymion, Endymion's Lab, Endymion Empire and the Pendulum scales in one go.

profile.plan: Special Summons DARK Winged Beast Blackwings from the hand and searches with Black Whirlwind and Sudri, Synchro Summoning into Black-Winged Dragon, Assault Blackwing monsters and a Blackwing Full Armor Master that is unaffected by other cards' effects.

weaknesses.label: Searches with Black Whirlwind
weaknesses.why: Black Whirlwind adds a Blackwing from the Deck on every Normal Summon and Sudri the Phantom Glimmer adds a card from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates those adds cuts the combo off at the first search.

weaknesses.label: Normal Summon monster effects
weaknesses.why: Sudri, Auster, Blizzard and Elphin all start the combo with an effect that triggers when they are Normal Summoned, so negating a face-up monster's effect ends the turn before any Synchro Summon.

weaknesses.label: Summons many monsters
weaknesses.why: The deck Special Summons Bora, Kris, Gale, Oroshi and others before Synchro Summoning, easily reaching five Summons in one turn, which lets cards that punish that many Summons wipe the board.

weaknesses.label: Synchro Summons from the Extra Deck
weaknesses.why: Every payoff, from Nothung and Raikiri to Black-Winged Dragon and Full Armor Master, is a Synchro Summon, so a floodgate that forbids Synchro Summons leaves the deck with only small Winged Beasts.

weaknesses.label: Unaffected boss monsters
weaknesses.why: Blackwing Full Armor Master is unaffected by other cards' effects while Onimaru cannot be destroyed by card effects and Armor Master cannot be destroyed by battle, so only cards that Tribute them or use them as material remove them going second.

weaknesses.label: Continuous Spell engine
weaknesses.why: Black Whirlwind and Black Feather Whirlwind are placed face-up from the Deck and carry the searching and Synchro support, so Spell/Trap removal on them cripples the engine.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Black Whirlwind's search or Sudri's add from the Deck, stopping the combo at its first search.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: After the first Black Whirlwind or Sudri search it stops every further add, starving the deck of Blackwings.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates Sudri, Auster, Blizzard or Elphin on the field before they can extend.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence

weaknesses.label: Graveyard revival

weaknesses.label: Continuous Spell/Trap support
weaknesses.why: Millennium Revelation, Sun God Unification and Ultimate Divine-Beast sit in the Spell & Trap Zone and carry the revive/attack support, so backrow removal strips it.

weaknesses.label: Protected boss

profile.plan: It destroys its own Dinosaurs to Special Summon from the Deck and Synchro Summon, ending on Astero's Summon negation and Volcano's Quick Effect Meteor board wipe.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field

weaknesses.label: Uses the GY as fuel

weaknesses.label: Special Summons many monsters

weaknesses.label: Ends on a Field Spell
weaknesses.why: Volcano protects Jurrac monsters by banishing Dinosaurs from the GY and summons Meteor after four opponent monster effects, so backrow removal takes away the end board's protection and Quick Effect.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a wide board

profile.plan: Searches Assault Mode Activate, Synchro Summons a base Synchro, then Tributes it with Assault Mode Activate to Special Summon an /Assault Mode boss from the Deck, ending on a large negating or board-wiping monster plus Assault Counter.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field

weaknesses.label: Tributes Synchro Monsters

weaknesses.label: Trap-based payoff
weaknesses.why: The deck's main play is resolving Assault Mode Activate, and Assault Counter is another Trap, so a card that negates Trap activation stops the whole turn.

weaknesses.label: Set backrow
weaknesses.why: Assault Mode Activate, Assault Counter and Assault Slash are Set Traps, so backrow removal clears the payoff and the negation before they can be used.

weaknesses.label: Ends on one big boss
weaknesses.why: Going second the board is usually a single /Assault Mode monster such as T.G. Halberd Cannon/Assault Mode or Arcanite Magician/Assault Mode plus Assault Counter, so non-targeting board breakers get through.

profile.plan: The deck Tributes a Synchro with its Trap to Special Summon a high-Level /Assault Mode boss from the Deck, ending on Stardust Dragon/Assault Mode's negate or Red Nova Dragon/Assault Mode's banish plus destruction floaters.

weaknesses.label: Trap-dependent Summoning
weaknesses.why: Every boss must be Special Summoned by the Trap that Tributes a Synchro and Summons from the Deck, so removing that set Trap before it activates leaves the deck unable to field a boss.

weaknesses.label: Searches and Summons from Deck
weaknesses.why: Crimson Blader/Assault Mode adds the Trap from the Deck and the Trap Special Summons the boss from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates Deck effects stops the setup.

weaknesses.label: On-field monster effects
weaknesses.why: Stardust Dragon/Assault Mode's negation, Red Nova Dragon/Assault Mode's banish and Black Rose Dragon/Assault Mode's board wipe are all face-up monster effects, so negating the monster turns them off.

weaknesses.label: Floats when destroyed
weaknesses.why: Each boss Special Summons its original Synchro from the GY when destroyed, so banishing, Tributing or bouncing the boss denies that replacement.

weaknesses.label: Trap activation is the choke point
weaknesses.why: The bosses only hit the field through one Trap's activation, so negating that activation stops the Summon before it happens.

weaknesses.label: GY-based floaters
weaknesses.why: The destruction floaters and Stardust Dragon/Assault Mode's End Phase revival use the GY, so banishing the original Synchro or the boss from the GY stops them returning.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Stardust Dragon/Assault Mode, Red Nova Dragon/Assault Mode or Black Rose Dragon/Assault Mode before their Quick Effects resolve.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster
answers.why: Destroys the set Trap before it can Summon a boss.

answers.name: Cosmic Cyclone

answers.name: Red Reboot

answers.name: Gameciel, the Sea Turtle Kaiju
answers.why: Tributing one boss removes it without destroying it and without triggering its float.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes the original Synchro or the boss from the GY so its destruction float or End Phase revival has no target.

weaknesses.label: Graveyard recursion

profile.plan: Morphtronic switches its Machine monsters between Attack and Defense to use position-dependent effects, using Celfon and Converter to Special Summon from the Deck and Telefon, Remoten and Repair Unit to recur from the GY, ending on Synchro monsters such as Earfon equipped to them.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field

weaknesses.label: Graveyard setup
weaknesses.why: Telefon and Repair Unit Special Summon from the GY, and Remoten and Smartfon banish from the GY, so making every send a banish cuts off the recursion.

weaknesses.label: Machine-Type engine

weaknesses.label: Summons many monsters

weaknesses.label: Synchro and Equip end board
weaknesses.why: The deck ends on Synchro monsters such as Earfon and Equip Cards attached to them, so a board breaker like Evenly Matched clears the whole setup going second.

profile.plan: Mills the opponent's Deck down to nothing, using Iron Chain Dragon's battle damage and Poison Chain's End Phase mill while Iron Chain Snake is equipped to your monsters so their destruction mills even more.

weaknesses.label: Mills from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Poison Chain's End Phase effect and Iron Chain Dragon's battle-damage trigger both send cards from the top of the opponent's Deck to the GY, so a hand trap that negates a send from the Deck cuts the mill before it happens.

weaknesses.label: Mill engine in the backrow
weaknesses.why: Poison Chain is a Continuous Spell that does the deck's main non-battle milling and Iron Chain Snake sits in the Spell & Trap Zone as an Equip Card, so Spell/Trap removal takes out both mill engines at once.

weaknesses.label: Rebuilds only from the GY
weaknesses.why: Iron Chain Repairman's once-per-turn Special Summon targets an Iron Chain monster in the GY and Iron Chain Dragon powers up by removing them from there, so attacking the GY leaves nothing to revive or use.

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Iron Chain Coil's ATK boost, Iron Chain Blaster's burn, Iron Chain Repairman's revival and Iron Chain Snake's equip are all effects of face-up monsters, so negating one on the field ends the play.

weaknesses.label: Wins by decking you out
weaknesses.why: Iron Chain Dragon, Poison Chain and the equipped Iron Chain Snake all empty the opponent's Deck, so a card that shuffles your own GY back into the Deck keeps it from ever running out of cards to draw.

weaknesses.label: Ends on a single Synchro
weaknesses.why: The deck's payoff is one Iron Chain Dragon plus Poison Chain, so a board breaker that clears the monster and the backrow going second removes the entire mill setup.

answers.name: Called by the Grave

answers.name: Necrovalley

answers.name: Lightning Storm
answers.why: Destroys Iron Chain Dragon and the backrow mill setup in one card going second.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons many times

weaknesses.label: Ends on an Extra Deck board

profile.plan: Special Summons Machine monsters from the hand, Deck and GY by discarding or banishing, ending on Machina Citadel and Machina Ruinforce with destruction and Battle Phase negation.

weaknesses.label: Needs Shining Sarcophagus

weaknesses.label: Every monster is a Dragon
weaknesses.why: Gandora-G, Gigarays, Gandora and Gandora-X are all Dragon-Type, so a floodgate allowing only one monster of each Type shuts off the deck's bodies.

weaknesses.label: Ends on one bare Dragon
weaknesses.why: The payoff is a single Gandora with ATK built from banished cards and no protection, so board breakers and mass removal clear it going second.

answers.name: Effect Veiler

answers.name: Forbidden Droplet

profile.plan: Batteryman swarms LIGHT Thunder monsters with Normal Summon effects that search and Special Summon from the Deck, then uses Graveyard recursion and Short Circuit to destroy the opponent's entire board.

weaknesses.label: Deck searching and Summoning
weaknesses.why: 9-Volt adds a Batteryman from the Deck while Charger and Micro-Cell Special Summon one from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates Deck effects stops the first play.

weaknesses.label: Normal Summon effects
weaknesses.why: Charger, 9-Volt and Solar all need their Summoned trigger to resolve, so negating a face-up monster's effect ends the turn early.

weaknesses.label: Graveyard recursion
weaknesses.why: Battery Charger, Quick Charger and Portable Battery Pack revive or add from the GY, and Industrial Strength banishes from the GY, so banishing those monsters removes the follow-up.

weaknesses.label: One Type and Attribute
weaknesses.why: Every monster is a LIGHT Thunder, so a floodgate allowing only one Type or Attribute leaves them with a single body and stops Short Circuit, Fuel Cell and the token swarm.

weaknesses.label: Wide Attack Position board
weaknesses.why: The deck ends on several Attack Position Batteryman to enable Short Circuit and Fuel Cell, so mass removal or a board breaker that clears monsters breaks it going second.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates 9-Volt's search, Charger's or Micro-Cell's Special Summon from the Deck, or Solar's send from the Deck to the GY.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every further add from the Deck after the first, cutting off the searches the deck chains together.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Charger, 9-Volt or Solar on the field before its trigger resolves.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first Batteryman monster effect on the field, usually the Normal Summon trigger that starts the combo.

answers.name: D.D. Crow
answers.why: Banishes a Batteryman in the GY so Battery Charger, Quick Charger or Portable Battery Pack has no target.

answers.name: Dimension Shifter
answers.why: Makes every card sent to the GY banished instead, turning off Solar's send and all the GY recursion.

answers.name: Rivalry of Warlords
answers.why: All its monsters are Thunder, so it can only keep one on the field, turning off Short Circuit and Fuel Cell.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Attack Position Batteryman board at the end of the Battle Phase, getting past their Short Circuit setup.

profile.plan: Searches HERO monsters with Stratos, Shadow Mist and E - Emergency Call, cheats bodies out with A Hero Lives and Neos Fusion, then Fusion Summons Sunrise, Absolute Zero and Shining Neos Wingman, linking through Cross Crusader and Wonder Driver for extra searches and recursion.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Stratos, Shadow Mist, E - Emergency Call, Xtra HERO Infernal Devicer and Cross Crusader all add HERO cards from the Deck, so a hand trap that negates the add stops the combo before any Fusion Summon.

weaknesses.label: Field monster effects
weaknesses.why: Stratos, Shadow Mist, Blazeman, Solid Soldier and Liquid Soldier all start the combo with an effect on the field, so negating a face-up monster's effect ends the turn before the Fusion Summon.

weaknesses.label: Constant Special Summons
weaknesses.why: A Hero Lives, Neos Fusion, Neo Space Connector, Hero Signal and the Xtra HERO Link Monsters all Special Summon, so a floodgate that forbids Special Summoning locks the deck out of its whole engine.

weaknesses.label: Multiple Attributes
weaknesses.why: Sunrise needs two HERO monsters with different Attributes and Absolute Zero, The Shining and Escuridao each need a specific Attribute, so a floodgate leaving only one Attribute on the field stops every Fusion Summon.

weaknesses.label: Summons five or more
weaknesses.why: A full combo Special Summons five or more times through A Hero Lives, Solid Soldier, Neo Space Connector and the Xtra HERO Links, so cards that punish that many Summons wipe the board mid-combo.

weaknesses.label: Fusion end board
weaknesses.why: It ends on Fusion Monsters like Sunrise and Shining Neos Wingman backed by Absolute Zero, whose leave-field effect wipes your monsters, so board breakers that remove without targeting or destruction are what gets through.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Stratos's or Shadow Mist's add from the Deck and A Hero Lives' Special Summon from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: Stops every search and draw after the first, cutting off the chain of HERO searches the deck needs.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates Stratos, Blazeman or Liquid Soldier on the field before it can search or revive.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first HERO monster's on-field effect, usually the Stratos or Shadow Mist that starts the combo.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributes the whole board once the combo has Summoned five or more monsters.

answers.name: Gozen Match
answers.why: Limits each player to one Attribute, which blocks the different-Attribute Fusion Summons Sunrise and the Attribute-specific Fusions need.

answers.name: Vanity's Emptiness
answers.why: Neither player can Special Summon, shutting off A Hero Lives, Neos Fusion, the Link Summons and every Fusion Summon.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the Fusion board face-down, dodging Absolute Zero's leave-field wipe and Shining Neos Wingman's destruction protection.

profile.plan: It destroys its own Nephthys cards with card effects so they come back in the next Standby Phase, Ritual Summons Cerulean Sacred Phoenix and Conductor with Rebirth of Nephthys, then Link Summons Sacred Preserver and Sacred Flame, ending on a protected Winged Beast board that destroys the opponent's monsters.

weaknesses.label: Searches and Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: Disciple of Nephthys adds a Nephthys monster from the Deck, Conductor of Nephthys Ritual Summons one straight from the Deck and Sacred Preserver adds a Level 8 Winged Beast, so a hand trap that negates Deck effects stops the first play.

weaknesses.label: Revives monsters from the GY
weaknesses.why: Sacred Phoenix, Cerulean, Matriarch and Devotee all Special Summon themselves out of the GY and Chronicler recovers from there, so banishing the Nephthys monster from the GY before the Standby Phase takes the recursion away.

weaknesses.label: Every effect moves cards out of the GY
weaknesses.why: The Standby Phase revivals, Matriarch's Summon and Chronicler's recovery all move cards out of the GY, so a floodgate that shuts the GY off ends the engine on the spot.

weaknesses.label: Adds several cards to hand
weaknesses.why: Disciple searches a monster, Sacred Preserver searches a Winged Beast and a Ritual Spell and Chronicler adds from the GY, so stopping every add after the first starves the combo of fuel.

weaknesses.label: Ignition effects on the field
weaknesses.why: Disciple, Defender, Matriarch and Chronicler all begin the combo with 'During your Main Phase' effects on the field, so negating a face-up monster stops the play before anything is Ritual Summoned.

weaknesses.label: Swarms to a big board
weaknesses.why: A full turn Ritual Summons with Rebirth of Nephthys, chains Conductor and Devotee into more Ritual Summons and then Link Summons Preserver and Sacred Flame, so it passes five or more Summons and can be Tributed away mid-combo.

answers.name: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring
answers.why: Negates Disciple's add from the Deck, Conductor's Ritual Summon from the Deck and Devotee's Special Summon from the Deck.

answers.name: Droll & Lock Bird
answers.why: After the first search it stops every further add, cutting off Disciple, Sacred Preserver and Chronicler.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence
answers.why: Negates the on-field Main Phase effect of Disciple, Defender, Matriarch or Chronicler.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates the first Nephthys monster's Ignition Effect before it destroys a card and searches or Summons.

answers.name: Called by the Grave
answers.why: Banishes a Nephthys monster from the GY so its Standby Phase revival and its GY effect never resolve.

answers.name: Necrovalley
answers.why: Cards in the GY cannot be moved, which turns off every revival, Matriarch's Summon and Chronicler's recovery.

answers.name: Nibiru, the Primal Being
answers.why: Tributes the whole Ritual and Link board once the combo has Summoned five or more monsters, ignoring Sacred Flame's protection.

answers.name: Evenly Matched
answers.why: Banishes the end board face-down without targeting, getting past Sacred Flame's protection.

profile.plan: Special Summons Silent Swordsman by Tributing a Warrior and climbs through the LV monsters, ending on Silent Swordsman LV7 negating all Spell effects while Silent Swordsman and Silent Paladin negate Spells.

weaknesses.label: Searches and Special Summons from Deck
weaknesses.why: Silent Paladin adds a LV monster from the Deck and Silent Sword Slash's GY effect adds a Silent Swordsman monster, while LV3 and LV5 Special Summon their upgrades from the Deck, so Ash Blossom negates the first search or Summon.

weaknesses.label: Spell negation is a monster effect
weaknesses.why: Silent Swordsman, Silent Paladin and Silent Swordsman LV7 stop Spells only through their own face-up monster effects, so negating those monsters turns off every Spell negation.

weaknesses.label: All monsters are LIGHT
weaknesses.why: Every Silent Swordsman monster and Silent Paladin is LIGHT, so Light-Imprisoning Mirror negates all of their effects, including the Spell negations and the LV upgrades.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons from Deck and hand
weaknesses.why: LV3 and LV5 Special Summon their upgrades from the Deck and Silent Swordsman summons another copy when destroyed, so Vanity's Emptiness stops the whole LV ladder.

weaknesses.label: Only stops Spell effects
weaknesses.why: Silent Swordsman LV7 negates all Spell effects but nothing stops Traps or monster effects, so a Trap board breaker like Evenly Matched clears the board.

weaknesses.label: Special Summon by Tributing a Warrior
weaknesses.why: Silent Swordsman can only be Special Summoned by Tributing a Warrior, so Mask of Restrict stops it from ever reaching the field.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence

answers.name: Mask of Restrict
answers.why: Neither player can Tribute, so Silent Swordsman cannot be Special Summoned by Tributing a Warrior.

profile.plan: Special Summons Machine-Type B.E.S. monsters from the hand and Deck, placing counters that protect them from battle, while B.E.F. Zelos searches Boss Rush and grants targeting and destruction protection.

weaknesses.label: Searches from the Deck

weaknesses.label: Monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: A Quick Effect adds or revives and another monster's Quick Effect destroys cards, so Effect Veiler or Infinite Impermanence shuts them down.

weaknesses.label: Protected by its Field Spell
weaknesses.why: The Field Spell makes its monsters untargetable and indestructible by card effects, so non-targeting board breakers like Evenly Matched get through.

profile.plan: Grinds a single Dragon up the Horus ladder: LV4 destroys a monster by battle and, in the End Phase, upgrades itself into LV6 and then LV8 from the Deck, ending on a 3000 ATK Spell-negating boss protected from targeting by Horus' Servant.

weaknesses.label: Only levels up by battle
weaknesses.why: Horus the Black Flame Dragon LV4 and LV6 must destroy a monster by battle during the turn to Special Summon the next form in the End Phase, so a floodgate that stops Level 4 or higher monsters from attacking leaves the whole ladder stuck.

weaknesses.label: Level-up Summons from the Deck
weaknesses.why: LV4 and LV6 Special Summon the next Horus from the hand or Deck with their End Phase effect, so a hand trap that negates a Special Summon from the Deck cuts the ladder before LV8 ever arrives.

weaknesses.label: Activated monster effects on the field
weaknesses.why: LV6's End Phase upgrade and LV8's Spell negation are both activated monster effects, so negating a face-up monster's effect stops the level-up and removes the Spell lock.

weaknesses.label: Protection only covers Spells
weaknesses.why: LV6 is unaffected by Spell effects and LV8 only negates Spell activations while Horus' Servant only blocks targeting, so a Tribute that does not target removes the boss past all of that.

weaknesses.label: Cannot answer Trap cards
weaknesses.why: Horus the Black Flame Dragon LV8 negates only Spell Cards, so a Trap board breaker that banishes or destroys the LV8 plus the Servant protecting it resolves untouched.

answers.why: Negates the End Phase Special Summon of LV6 or LV8 from the Deck, so the ladder never reaches its boss.

answers.name: Effect Veiler
answers.why: Negates LV6's End Phase upgrade or LV8's Spell negation on the field.

answers.name: Infinite Impermanence

answers.name: Skill Drain
answers.why: Negates LV6's End Phase Summon and LV8's negation, reducing the deck to vanilla beaters.

answers.name: Gravity Bind

answers.name: Gameciel, the Sea Turtle Kaiju
answers.why: Tributing it for Gameciel removes LV6 or LV8 without targeting and without being a Spell.

answers.name: Evenly Matched

weaknesses.label: Banishes from the Graveyard

weaknesses.label: Ends on a protected board
weaknesses.why: Armed Dragon Lightning and Ojama Pajama protect the monsters and Thunder LV10 has a Quick Effect, so going-second board breakers such as Evenly Matched and Harpie's Feather Duster clear the board and its protection.

answers.name: Harpie's Feather Duster

profile.plan: Tributes its own monsters to Summon the Maju Garzett beatsticks, whose ATK becomes the combined original ATK of everything Tributed, alongside a Gren Maju Da Eiza that grows with the banished pile, ending on one or two huge Fiends — Emperor Maju Garzett also shuts off the opponent's cards and effects for the whole Battle Phase.

weaknesses.label: Everything runs on Tributes
weaknesses.why: Maju Garzett, Great Maju Garzett, Legendary Maju Garzett and Emperor Maju Garzett all gain their ATK only from monsters Tributed for them, so a card that forbids Tributing leaves them as 0 ATK bodies that cannot even be Summoned.

weaknesses.label: ATK set by a continuous effect
weaknesses.why: Maju Garzett, Great Maju Garzett, Legendary Maju Garzett, Emperor Maju Garzett and Gren Maju Da Eiza all set their ATK with their own effect, so negating face-up monster effects turns every one of them into a 0 ATK monster.

weaknesses.label: All its monsters are Fiend
weaknesses.why: Gren Maju Da Eiza and every Garzett is a Fiend, so a floodgate that allows only one monster of each Type leaves the deck unable to keep the two or three monsters it must Tribute.

weaknesses.label: Special Summons from the hand
weaknesses.why: Legendary Maju Garzett and Emperor Maju Garzett must be Special Summoned from the hand by Tributing, so negating that Summon stops the deck's biggest monster before it ever reaches the field.

weaknesses.label: One unprotected giant monster
weaknesses.why: The Garzetts have no protection from card effects at all, so going second a single removal effect or a Kaiju simply takes the huge ATK monster off the field in the Main Phase, before Emperor Maju Garzett's Battle Phase lock matters.

answers.name: Skill Drain

answers.name: Mask of Restrict

answers.name: There Can Be Only One
answers.why: Every monster in the deck is a Fiend, so they can only keep one on the field and can never gather the Tributes the bosses need.
